label: Emerging discipline
summary: Emerging discipline is how Maaike characterises conversation design: a field that is still maturing, without fully solidified standard practices, tools, or workflows. Because the discipline is not yet established, practitioners face ongoing challenges around inconsistent tooling, undefined processes, and difficulty communicating the value of their work to stakeholders.
how_maaike_uses: Maaike uses the concept of conversation design as an emerging discipline to explain several of the top challenges her Convoclub community reports. The immaturity of the field shows up in perceived knowledge gaps that affect designers at every experience level, in tools and analytics that have not yet standardised, and in the constant effort required to educate clients and leaders about what conversation designers actually do and why it matters. She frames the emerging status not as a reason for pessimism but as a call to action: designers should contribute to tool evolution, advocate for better processes, and push vendors to involve them in building the very platforms they use.
open_questions: When, if ever, will standard practices in conversation design fully solidify, and what would that actually look like?
Will the rapid arrival of LLMs accelerate or further delay the maturation of conversation design as a discipline?
